references.text: In [ref:Matt 28:2|Matthew 28:2], it is described that an angel came down from heaven and rolled the stone away from the tomb. This is the parallel account to Luke's description of the stone being rolled away from the tomb.
[ref:Mark 16:4|Mark 16:4] is Mark's parallel account where the women look up and discover that the stone has been rolled away from the tomb, even though it was very large.
In [ref:Joh 20:1|John 20:1], John tells us that Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed. This is the Johannine parallel to the same event.

In [ref:Matt 27:60|Matthew 27:60], it is described how Joseph of Arimathea rolled a large stone in front of the entrance to the tomb when Jesus was buried. Luke 24:2 refers to this stone now being rolled away.

[ref:Mark 15:46|Mark 15:46] tells us that Joseph of Arimathea rolled a stone in front of the entrance to the tomb after the burial. The rolled-away stone in Luke 24:2 is the same stone that was placed there.

In [ref:Mark 16:3|Mark 16:3], the women ask each other on their way to the tomb: "Who will roll the stone away from the entrance of the tomb for us?" This shows that the stone was a practical obstacle they did not expect to find removed.
In [ref:Luk 23:53|Luke 23:53], Luke himself tells us that Jesus was laid in a tomb cut out of rock. Luke 24:2 continues this story by describing what the women found when they returned to this tomb.
